inputs.reserve_composition: €6,000,000 government bonds, €3,000,000 commercial paper, €1,000,000 cash equivalents

result.test_failed: Article 32(3) full-backing requirement — reserve assets must at all times be at least equal to aggregate claims from token holders

article_basis: Article 32(3) Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA): 'Their aggregated value shall be at least equal to the aggregate value of the claims on the issuer from holders of asset-referenced tokens in circulation.'
tail_convention: Coverage ratio is a higher-is-better metric; the LOW tail is adverse. This test examines the adverse tail by testing whether coverage falls below the 100% threshold.
weakest_point: The reserve valuation assumes orderly mark-to-market pricing; if commercial paper becomes illiquid, the realisable value may fall below the €9.8M mark, deepening the shortfall beyond the €200,000 accounting deficit.

article_basis: Article 35(1) Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA): issuers of asset-referenced tokens shall at all times have own funds equal to at least the highest of (a) EUR 350,000, (b) 2% of the average amount of the reserve of assets, (c) a quarter of the fixed overheads of the preceding year.
tail_convention: Own-funds adequacy is a higher-is-better metric; the LOW tail is adverse. This test examines the adverse tail by testing whether actual own funds fall below the required minimum.
weakest_point: For this issuer the fixed floor (€350,000) dominates the percentage test (€200,000); the percentage test only becomes binding when average reserve assets exceed €17,500,000. A regulator applying the wrong test sequence or omitting the fixed floor could understate requirements by 42.9%.

result.test_failed: Article 32(3) full-backing requirement under stress — reserve assets after haircuts are insufficient to cover aggregate claims

article_basis: Article 32(3) and Article 35(5) Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA): issuers shall conduct stress testing; based on outcomes, competent authorities may require own funds 20%–40% higher than the Article 35(1)(b) amount.
tail_convention: Coverage ratio is a higher-is-better metric; the LOW tail is adverse. This stress test examines the adverse tail by applying haircuts that reduce reserve value toward the lower tail.
weakest_point: The haircuts are applied asset-by-asset without correlation; in a systemic liquidity crisis, government bonds and commercial paper may simultaneously gap down, producing a joint tail worse than the sum of individual haircuts.

result.test_satisfied: Full backing maintained post-redemption; redemption obligation met at par per EMT framework

article_basis: Article 54 Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA) reiterates Directive 2009/110/EC obligations for e-money tokens: funds received must be safeguarded and redeemable at par value in the referenced currency.
tail_convention: Redemption obligation magnitude is adverse to issuer solvency when high; the HIGH tail (large redemption requests) is adverse. This case examines the adverse tail by testing a material redemption request against the reserve.
weakest_point: The case assumes the issuer draws down reserve pro rata; if the issuer instead liquidates the most liquid assets first, the residual reserve becomes concentrated in less liquid instruments, raising liquidity risk for subsequent redemptions.
